column1: # Ancient Egyptian for the "Write in ..." tool (scribe.js); built by scripts/make-scribe.ps1.
# Hieroglyphs by their Gardiner numbers (the Unicode names: G001 is the vulture). Values: the Egyptological
# transliteration (ꜣ i y ꜥ w b p f m n r h ḥ ḫ ẖ z s š q k g t ṯ d ḏ); the typed forms after them are the letters a
# reader types for a name, after the way the Ptolemaic scribes spelt Greek names (Kleopatra: q-l-i-w-p-ꜣ-d-r-ꜣ-t), a
# convention, not a rule of Egyptian: vowels were not written in Egyptian words. Word signs and determinatives are typed
# in brackets: [ꜥnḫ] or [ankh], [woman]. ( and ) are the ends of a cartouche.

column4: Egyptian was written in hieroglyphs for more than 3,000 years: pictures that stand for sounds, for whole words, or, at the end of a word, for its kind of meaning; the vowels were never written.

column2: The sacred script of Egypt, from about 3200 BCE to the last inscription at Philae in 394 CE; scribes also wrote faster hands, hieratic and demotic, and the Rosetta Stone let Champollion read it again in 1822.

Type a name letter by letter: each sound becomes its one-sound sign, spelt the way Ptolemaic scribes spelt Greek names such as Cleopatra (a is the vulture, e and i the reed, o and u the quail chick; Egyptian itself did not write vowels). Word signs and determinatives go in brackets: [ankh], [nefer], [woman]. Put a royal name between ( and ) for a cartouche.

column4: vulture · a glottal stop; a in names
reed · i, y; e or i in names
arm · a sound squeezed in the throat
quail chick · w; o or u in names
lion · l in names of the Greek age
hill slope · k, deep in the throat
